title: Contractive Riesz projection conjecture and its endpoint logarithmic inequality
statement:
Let $P$ denote the Riesz projection from $L^2(\mathbb{T})$ onto $H^2$, and let $r$ and $q$ satisfy

$$
1<r\leq\infty,\qquad q=4\left(1-\frac{1}{r}\right).
$$

**Riesz projection contractivity conjecture.** The operator $P$ is a contraction from $L^r(\mathbb{T})$ to $H^q$. In addition, for every $f\in L^1(\mathbb{T})$,

$$
\exp\left(\int_0^{2\pi}\log|Pf(e^{i\theta})|\,\frac{d\theta}{2\pi}\right)\leq\|f\|_{L^1}.
$$

This conjecture connects the coefficient inequalities with contractive bounds for the Riesz projection. The source notes the endpoint $L^\infty(\mathbb{T})\to H^4$ result and its sharpness, but does not resolve the full asserted family or the accompanying $L^1$ inequality.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.00738

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2017).
source_name: Ole Fredrik Brevig, Joaquim Ortega-Cerdà, Kristian Seip and Jing Zhao, “Contractive inequalities for Hardy spaces”, arXiv:1706.00738 (2018).
